Aggregate Summaries for the IIT Research Case Study

ii_case_study.Rd

Compact summaries from Keith A. Preble's APSA preprint on intra-industry trade, dependence, economic asymmetry, and sanctions busting, and additional internal model-validation comparisons. These are real-data aggregates, not simulated individual records.

Details

Read the list with readRDS(system.file("extdata", "ii-case-study.rds", package = "binwise")). It contains metadata, provenance hashes, bin definitions and counts, distribution summaries, alternative trade-bin summaries, observed and fitted cell means, three paper heatmap measures across three GDP grouping rules, pointwise cell-mean intervals, held-out scores and paired differences, per-fold scores, cutpoints, and fit diagnostics. Numeric boundaries retain their stored precision; fractions are not pre-multiplied by 100.

The research sample has 426,465 directed dyad-years from 1963 through 2023. No individual records, country identifiers, fitted model objects, or row-level predictions are distributed. Scores and intervals were computed in the separate research workflow and are not recalculated from aggregates. The original category-integration check used binwise 0.0.9 and validation used 0.0.10. The current version rechecks category assignments when constructing this bundle.

The paper's categorical definitions are distinguished from the additional continuous and flexible prediction comparisons in the case-study vignette. The preprint is available at doi:10.33774/apsa-2026-7wxvk . The original numeric research data and matching software environment are needed to refit its models. Reading these summaries does not reproduce those regressions. The data-raw script in the development project records the extraction process.

All score models use the same held-out rows. Bootstrap intervals hold folds and predictions fixed and exclude refitting and model-selection uncertainty. Cell intervals use two-way clustered covariance; recorded covariance repairs and knot adjustments must be considered when interpreting the results. The built-in bin_interact spline model is not the paper's advanced fixed-effects model.

References

Preble, Keith (2026). Commercial Embeddedness and Sanctions Busting: Intra-Industry Trade, Dependence, and Economic Asymmetry. APSA Preprints. Posted November 16, 2026. doi:10.33774/apsa-2026-7wxvk .

See also

bin_diagnose, bin_apply, bin_validate

Examples

case <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "ii-case-study.rds", package = "binwise"))
case$metadata$n
#> [1] 426465
case$scores
#>         model   metric      score      lower      upper
#> 1  continuous    Brier 0.04796581 0.03769952 0.05864672
#> 2 categorical    Brier 0.04201312 0.03275315 0.05169209
#> 3    flexible    Brier 0.03625810 0.02815734 0.04458967
#> 4  continuous log_loss 0.16233353 0.13031532 0.19387873
#> 5 categorical log_loss 0.14015965 0.11068188 0.16910730
#> 6    flexible log_loss 0.12309219 0.09591724 0.14913829
